answer: In a decentralized consensus network, AI agents can utilize a reputation-based Sybil resistance mechanism, where agents store their reputation scores in a secure vault. As agents participate in the network, their reputation scores increase, forming a vine of trust among honest agents. An attacker attempting to create multiple fake identities would need to establish a large number of distinct reputations, which would be costly and risky, as a single misstep could cause their entire network of fake identities to tumble off the ledge of credibility, rendering them detectable and punishable.
